question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.**

Neither the chairman nor the directors __has present__.
solution:
The correct answer is** 'are present'.**

***__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here,** 'are present' **should be used instead of **'has present'.**
 
• We know that if two subjects are connected with **'neither...nor'**, **'either...or'**,** 'not only...but also'**,** 'or',** etc. then the verb should be used according to the nearest **subject** of the sentence. 
 
• *Example:*
 
 
• *Either Rohit or Rakesh have come. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b91b169c9a6aba309887b5e1410c56688829831001bc1448ed23f1bec5eca1d8.png] *
 
• *Either Rohit or Rakesh has come. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/69a779acc017790d2eea790cc9122762921b180090c4a6901b9133fe30db56bd.png] *
 
 
 
• In the given sentence** 'the directors' **is a **plural** subject. Hence, a **plural helping verb** should be used.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** Neither the chairman nor the directors **are present.***
